Article.ArticleTitle: Minocycline plus N-acetylcysteine reduce behavioral deficits and improve histology with a clinically useful time window.

Abstract.AbstractText: There are presently no drugs to treat traumatic brain injury (TBI). A major problem in developing therapeutics is that drugs to treat TBI lack sufficient potency when dosed within a clinically relevant time window. Previous studies have shown that minocycline (MINO, 45mg/kg) plus N-acetylcysteine (NAC, 150mg/kg) synergistically improved cognition and memory, modulated inflammation and prevented loss of oligodendrocytes that remyelinated damaged white matter when first dosed 1 hour (h) after controlled cortical impact (CCI) in rats.1, 2 We show that MINO (45mg/kg) plus NAC (150mg/kg) also prevents brain injury in a mouse closed head injury (CHI) TBI model. Using the CHI model, the concentrations of MINO and NAC were titrated to determine that MINO (22.5mg/kg) plus NAC (75mg/kg) was more potent than the original formulation. MINO (22.5mg/kg) plus NAC (75mg/kg) also limited injury in the rat CCI model. The therapeutic time window of MINO plus NAC was then tested in the CHI and CCI models. Mice and rats could acquire an active place avoidance task when MINO plus NAC was first dosed at 12h post-injury. A first dose at 12h also limited gray matter injury in the hippocampus and preserved myelin in multiple white matter tracts. Mice and rats acquired Barnes maze when MINO plus NAC was first dosed at 24h post-injury. These data suggest that MINO (22.5mg/kg) plus NAC (75mg/kg) remain potent when dosed at clinically useful time windows. Both MINO and NAC are FDA-approved drugs and have been safely administered to patients in clinical trials at the doses in the new formulation. This suggests that the drug combination of MINO plus NAC may be effective in treating TBI.
